known.title: The loop replay ends when the keyed defects are fixed and leaves valid extra findings unfixed, so it cannot measure the rounds and time of the production repair loop
known.locator: Research, Decisions, decision 3 (line 54); decision 6 (line 57); Goal (lines 7 and 13)
known.summary: Decision 3 ends a loop when a round matches no remaining known defect or when every known defect is fixed, and marks valid extra findings as accepted without a fix in the previous-round file. Production repairs every reproduced finding, also a LOW extra, and reviews again until no finding is open (plan-lifecycle yolo SKILL.md verdict table: fix each reproduced finding and review again; the code-reviewer delta reference repeats unfixed findings as open). So when round 1 finds every keyed defect plus a valid extra, the replay skips both the extra's repair and the confirming round, and understates the loop rounds and time that the Goal asks to measure (and the extra rounds that decision 6 wants to count). The key should score the run, not end the loop; extras need a repair.

known.title: Every follow-up round of the replay is a delta round, but production allows a delta round only under the contract's eligibility conditions and else runs a panel or full round
known.summary: Decision 2 claims the production reviewer setup with delta rounds for repairs, and decision 3 runs a delta round after every repair unconditionally. plan-contract.md (Code-review rounds) makes round k a delta round only when round k-1 completed, every change since its head repairs a finding of round k-1 or of the self-review, and the delta diff is at most half the full diff; otherwise round k is a panel or full round by the round-1 size rule. For a repair over that threshold, the replay runs a delta round where production runs panel or full, so it measures another review scope and cost than the production setup it claims to reproduce.

known.title: The held-out keys move outside the repository, but no step changes score.mjs readKnown and pairs to read keys from there, so held-out pair generation fails
known.locator: Research, Decisions, decision 1 (line 52); Steps, rows 2 scorer_report, 3 loop_replay, and 4 corpus (lines 78-80)
known.summary: Decision 1 keeps the held-out keys outside the repository ($XDG_STATE_HOME/docks/review-bench/keys/) during the runs, but no step assigns the scorer migration. score.mjs readKnown, which pairsCommand calls, reads only the inline known list or the <id>.key.json next to the case file, and the pairs command takes only --cases. With the keys outside the repository, pair generation for held-out cases (and the loop replay that needs the keys) fails before judging. Steps 2 and 3 need an external key lookup (for example a keys-folder option) in the scorer and the loop, and references/judge.md needs to describe that key input.

known.title: The Goal asks for the time and defects found per round, but the report of decision 4 gives only round-1 numbers and loop totals
known.locator: Goal (line 7); Research, Decisions, decision 4 (line 55); Steps, row 2 scorer_report (line 78)
known.summary: The Goal requires the report to show, for each configuration, the time and the defects found per round. Decision 4 lists round-1 time and round-1 defects found plus loop aggregates (rounds, loop time, defects found by the end, escaped), and no row gives the time or the defects found of round 2, 3, and later; step 2 assigns no round-indexed scores or timing, and the existing score.mjs report rows identify repetitions (runs), not rounds within a loop. A three-round loop therefore need not show what its later rounds found or cost.
